title: A Simple, Nearly-Optimal Algorithm for Differentially Private All-Pairs Shortest Distances

predicted_errors.error_location: Theorem 4.3 proof, Eq. (3), and Theorem 4.4 proof
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The algorithm runs each tree with privacy parameter ε/(t·k), where t = ⌈100 n^{1/k} log n⌉ and there are |T| = t·k trees. By Corollary 4.1 the additive error per tree scales like 1/(per-tree ε), so the union-bound error must scale with t·k = O(k n^{1/k} log n), not k n^{1/k}. Equation (3) writes the error as O(k n^{1/k} log^{1.5} n log(n t k/γ)/ε), omitting the factor t, and therefore understates the explicit polylogarithmic dependence by at least a factor of log n. The same issue affects the approximate-DP version.

The proof claims that because w ∈ B(v) and, 'by equivalent logic', w ∈ B(u), both u and v lie in the same cluster C^m(w). However, Lemma 4.5 only gives the needed inequality when w is the closest vertex to the target in A_i^r. The bunch condition w ∈ B(v) means only d(w,v) < d(v,p_{i+1}(v)); it does not imply that w is closer to v than every other center in A_i^r. A different center in the same subset A_i^r could be closer to v, in which case v ∉ C^m(w). Thus the existence of a tree T* with d_{T*}(u,v) = d(w,u)+d(w,v) is not established.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.2 swapping procedure and Theorem 4.3 proof
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The query algorithm can terminate at i=0 with w = u. The constructed collection T consists only of trees built from centers in A_i for i ∈ [k−1]; no level-0 trees are constructed. The proof of Theorem 4.3 nevertheless assumes the final w satisfies w ∈ A_l^m for some l ∈ [k−1], so the i=0 base case is unhandled.

The proof states 'Let X_i ∼ Binomial(n,p_i)' for the number of vertices in A_i. But A_i is the union of t fixed-size random subsets sampled without replacement; the inclusion indicators of different vertices are dependent. For t=1, X_i is deterministic, not binomial. Thus the claimed Binomial distribution is false, and the Chernoff bound is not justified as stated.

The proofs say each tree is run with ε/(2√2(k n^{1/k}) log(2/δ))-DP (and analogously with t·k), which as written has M = k n^{1/k} and log(2/δ) outside the square root. Advanced composition requires per-mechanism privacy ε/(2√{2M log(2/δ)}). The written expression would make the additive error scale with M log(2/δ) rather than √{M log(2/δ)}, contradicting the claimed O(√M...) error. The intended expression appears to have a missing square root.
